matches.note: Announced as a match between Frost, Sabbot and Tragic Hero against Chris Camero, and remade into a four-way from the ring after Jason Dynasty put Camero through a glass window backstage for refusing him a title shot. Tragic Hero spent the opening of it absent and Dynasty spent it fighting Leviathan in a corridor.

Salaok came out first and announced there would be no match, Brick having no-showed; Logan Creed put Brick on the speakerphone on the Globaltron, and Brick drove a Lincoln Navigator into the arena. Kullypso cut the cell's padlock and both Harvesters came in to save Salaok and were put down. Brick won it with the Bricklayer onto the overturned steel steps. West introduces Salaok twice, at 156 lbs "because that is what his bio reads" and at 256, and the whole introduction runs twice over.

Non-title, and fought on a rooftop across the road from the arena, shot from a helicopter. Quartz called his son Shale and asked him to come home to the Harvesters; Silent Wind told him Shale was dead, and detonated the building. No decision was announced. Quartz was pulled alive out of the rubble; what the cameras found of Silent Wind was a torn and slashed black mask.

notes: The fed's own biggest night, and the last show of its own that the record holds. Two of its ten matches are fought outside the building — the opener in the car park and the main event on a rooftop across the road — and neither is given a decision. It crowns the first PrimeStar Champion in a one-night tournament, changes the Platinum title, and settles the fed's own two long arcs: Brick beats the co-owner who had spent months trying to fire him, and Silent Wind blows up a building with his father in it. The opening video spells the show's name out one letter at a time as WRESTLECADE III; Ben J. Pailthorpe calls it WrestleCade 2003 from the ring.

It is "the return of Global Overload" and says "Fusion returns Next week with a Massive Night of Champions card"; Fusion Night of Champions is dated 15 February 2007, so the show falls the week before it, and 8 February 2007 is the Thursday of that week. No source states the day.

Global Wrestling's own write-up (accession 0159, booking 2113), dated jointly with Argyle's side. It carries no dateline. It follows the Fusion of 8 October 2007, which ended with the ladder match for ownership of Global ("Last week we found out that the man who has ran this ship for years no longer owns this company"), and precedes the Fusion of 23 October 2007, whose card the PTC forum's Fed and Character News board posted on the evening of 17 October. 17 October is the day the results were posted; the Fusions either side of it that this wing holds fall on a Monday (8 October) and a Tuesday (23 October), so the show's own night may be 15 October. No source states the day.

date.source: Global Wrestling's own write-up (accession 0159, booking 2280), dated jointly with Argyle's side. It carries no dateline, but two dated posts put its airing on the evening of Friday 6 February 2004 in the United States: Global's own news post (Underground results, post 25 of 30 in file order) was archived at 06:12 UTC on 7 February (22:12 on 6 February Pacific time), and the PTC forum's "Global Wrestling Overload is now airing." was posted at 07:29 UTC the same morning; it says this Overload "was thrown off a night by a special TV series marathon", which moves its Thursday slot to the Friday.
